Registration (main session): build the candidate image, run the container wiring smoke below, then copy 'plan' into gsp07-v1-plan.json and this document into gsp07-v1-protocol.json with 'registered_at_utc', 'source' (commit, server/app manifest) and 'image' (tag, id) filled and the four script hashes recomputed from the registered commit. Every open question is closed below; 'to_fill_at_registration' lists the only blanks.
item: SP07: C0 = legacy (indexer_cache_hard_ttl_seconds 0 = today's tracker cache; breaker off, Tech Info prefetch off) vs C7 = swr (hard TTL 86400 s = 24 h, the user's UX/SLO decision, row 5; indexer_cache_refresh_max_in_flight 4, the code default; breaker off, prefetch off). The soft TTL is the product's 1800 s, shortened in-process to 20 s by the harness (--imdb-cache-ttl) in both arms.

harness.what_is_real: API-key/DB auth, Stremio/provider/repository path, IndexerSearchService with the SP07 tracker IMDb cache (soft/hard TTL, per-key background refresh, forced refresh on 0 playable streams, owner/lifespan), shared source search (singleflight incl. the imdb-fresh key, deadline, .torrent download/store), Tech Info enrichment, filter/sort/serialization.
harness.what_is_synthetic: tracker adapters (latency with per-tracker jitter streams; a new release per tracker after the warm request in mu/ep), .torrent download latency, nCore-like Tech Info stub. No real tracker, account or network; external HTTP is blocked and counted.
harness.rows: stale = same IMDb id (ep: S01E02) --stale-after s after its cold request, stream response cache invalidated, tracker entry soft-expired; followup = the same request once every background refresh settled; tracker_calls = synthetic tracker searches from the request start until its background refreshes settled; new_upload_visible = the new release's torrent identity (bingeGroup '<indexer>-<torrent id>' ending in '-new' / containing '-ep2-') is among the playable streams

runner: scripts/run_sp_search_gate.py (unchanged): one fresh --network none container per run (cpuset 0,1, 2 CPU, 1 GiB); per repetition the variant order and the arm order rotate, both arms of a variant back to back; repetition r uses --seed 20261112 + r for both arms; 2 series x 5 repetitions x 3 variants x 2 arms = 60 runs.
time_note: Time scale 1 (the product's 1.5 s Tech Info budget is an unscaled code constant). Per run: 24 cold requests every 6 s, each with an immediate warm pair; the stale event of cold i is due at 6 i + 30 s and runs after the pair due at the same time, followed by its followup; the last stale event is due at 168 s. gsp06-v1 (same 24 x 6 s schedule, same image family) took 141-145 s wall per run, so ~172 s per run here and ~2 h 55 min for the 60 runs. Each 6 s slot holds at most one cold+warm pair (~1 s) and one stale+followup pair (C0 ~1 s, C7 ~0.6 s), so the schedule does not drift.
why_seed_per_rep: As in GSP06: both arms of a repetition see the same per-tracker jitter sequence (C7's background refresh takes the draw C0's synchronous refresh takes, in the same order; the forced refresh of ep joins it and draws nothing), repetitions sample different sequences, so the bootstrap over repetitions includes the sequence variance.

expected_mechanism.m: C0 drops the soft-expired entry, so the stale request waits a full tracker search (~0.4 s + jitter); C7 serves the old list at once (~warm path) and refreshes each tracker once in the background. Tracker calls 3 per stale request and 0 per followup in both arms; identical torrents and rendered streams in every row.
expected_mechanism.mu: C0's stale request refetches, sees the new release and downloads its .torrent; C7's stale request serves the old list (no new release, by design: the accepted staleness, bounded by the next request and the 24 h hard TTL), the background refresh lands it and the followup shows it (and downloads it). Stale rows differ by design; cold, warm and followup rows carry the same torrents.
expected_mechanism.ep: C0's synchronous refetch finds S01E02. C7's old list has 0 playable streams for S01E02, so find_by_imdb asks a forced (allow_stale=False) refresh before the name fallback; it joins the background refresh the same request started, so still 3 tracker calls. Identical torrents in every row; the stale request costs C7 one extra pass over the old list (see the margin).

wiring_smoke_in_process: Not a measurement (this branch, in-process, no Docker; --smoke --scenarios S1 --requests 3 --interval 2 --time-scale 0.2 --imdb-cache-ttl 3 --stale-after 4 --steady-from 0, legacy vs swr, n = 3 per kind; ms in unscaled units): one process per policy and variant (as the runner does), --seed 20261112. Steady p50, C0 -> C7: m stale 583 -> 40 ms (warm 40/41), mu stale 796 -> 41 ms, ep stale 916 -> 933 ms (p95 973 -> 1010; at time scale 0.2 the reported ms are 5x the real cost, so the real extra is ~3.5/7.5 ms); cold, warm and followup about equal. The draft rule run through decide_sp_search_gate.py on these 6 runs: 0 digest mismatches (source_set_digest; m and ep every kind, mu cold/warm/followup), 0 enrichment mismatches (m), 0 new_upload_violations, 0 tracker_call_violations (3 per stale, 0 per followup in both arms), no tracker_call_check violation; the improve/guard lists are meaningless at n = 1 and were ignored. 0 external HTTP attempts. Two policies in one process get different IMDb ids (run_index), so identity checks need one policy per process.

decision_rule.machine_rule: scripts/decide_sp_search_gate.py (sha256 at registration); uses the opt-in keys per-entry margin, identical_sources_by_kind, require_new_upload_visible, max_tracker_calls_per_request and max_extra_tracker_calls_per_request, which leave gsp05-v1 and gsp06-v1 decisions unchanged (checked)
decision_rule.statistic: per-run steady-window (cold requests 2..23 and their warm/stale/followup rows) latency p50/p95 (ms); pooled n = 10 runs per arm and variant; difference of means; 10 000 bootstrap resamples, seed 20261113; one-sided p-values; Holm per family at alpha 0.05

guard_margin_reasons.default 0 ms: every other latency guard compares paths both arms run alike (cold, warm, m followup, ep cold/warm/followup) or that C7 must not worsen (m/mu stale p95): no tolerated worsening, as in GSP05/GSP06
guard_margin_reasons.ep stale 50 ms: by design C7 makes one extra pass over the old list before joining the refresh (account read, cache read, snapshot lookup, stream resolution: about one warm-path request; gsp06-v1, same schedule and time scale: warm p50 10.4-10.9 ms, p95 11.3-11.5 ms). 50 ms allows ~4 such passes and is ~5% of a C0 episode stale request (0.4 s tracker search + 0.2 s downloads + Tech Info); a larger cost means the forced path does more than intended.

pass_if_all: both improvements significant after Holm: m and mu stale steady p50 lower
no guard regression after Holm over the 20 latency guards (ep stale p50/p95 with a 50 ms margin, the rest 0)
identical torrent identity (source_set_digest) per (kind, index) across all runs of both arms in m and ep (every kind) and in mu (cold, warm, followup); identical rendered streams in m
the new release is visible in every mu followup row and every ep stale and followup row of both arms
every stale and followup row of both arms makes at most 3 tracker calls (one per tracker), and C7's mean per kind is not above C0's
descriptive_only: mu stale new-release visibility (0 in C7 by design)

mu followup latency and Tech Info enrichment (the new release's .torrent is downloaded at the followup in C7, at the stale request in C0; the product enriches the first 5 torrents in source order, and the new release lands at a different position)

closed_questions.time_scale: 1, as GSP06: the Tech Info budget is unscaled and the reported ms stay comparable with gsp06; ~2 h 55 min.
closed_questions.ep_stale_latency: guarded with a 50 ms per-entry margin (reason above), not descriptive.
closed_questions.hard_checks: opt-in keys in scripts/decide_sp_search_gate.py; with those keys absent gsp05-v1 and gsp06-v1 decide exactly as before (gsp06-v1 byte-identical to the committed decision; gsp05-v1 decision, lists and all n/p-values identical, the committed file predating the 622d802 output format).

Outside this gate's measurement (the H2 harness drives the Stremio path only).
